groups.activity: Exterminate; wake and kill the dormant Void Angel, then sweep the map

rows.label: Voidplume Pinion
rows.note: build requirement; one per dormant Void Angel

rows.label: Voidplume Quill
rows.alt: bounties, Zarium Accolades at Melica consoles, or Ravenous Angels

rows.label: Thrax Plasm
rows.note: Thrax Centurions and Legatus; passively covered while farming Pinions

conditions: Rank 1 (Fallen) costs 5,000 standing plus 5 Voidplume Down, 2,000 Ferrite, 2,000 Alloy Plate and 10,000 credits.
The daily cap is 16,000 + 500 per Mastery Rank, so ~23,000 at MR14 — Rank 1's pool and the blueprint both fit in one day once plumes are in hand.
Ravenous Angels (end of Void Armageddon) are not dormant Angels: they have 2 health bars and drop Quills, not Pinions. Dormant Angels have 3 bars.
Blast damage (+75%, Machinery health) is the single most repeated combat tip; aim for the head, which is a real weak point.
After the first health bar, stop meleeing — the Angel's near-invisible red mist heals it off any damage it deals you. Self-healing specters (Nidus) are the worst offender.
bonuses: Madurai Void Strike can burst the Ethereal form's shield fast enough to skip the invulnerability-orb phase entirely; two Madurai users can each pop it once to carry a squad through both void phases.
Void Sling through a gold orb for a dome shield that roughly doubles amp damage and blocks the laser sweep and charge beam; don't stack domes.
Lost Spirits run to the nearest Voidplume, Accolade, or Somachord fragment — Volt's Speed makes them run faster — though they won't lead to the dormant Angel or a Melica console.

Halako Perimeter (Exterminate) is the near-unanimous pick: no fail state, unlimited time, and the Angel reliably spawns in one of a few big-room tiles. A bounty stage naming 'Awaken a Dormant Void Angel' gives a waypoint instead of a search.

disclosures.title: Nekros/Hydroid looting is dead advice
disclosures.body: Desecrate and Pilfering Swarm duplicating Voidplume Pinions was patched out in Hotfix 31.5.4 (May 2022); threads repeating it since are wrong.

rows.label: Entrati Lanthorn
rows.note: guaranteed per Netracell run, and keeps dropping past the 5-run weekly cap
rows.alt: Gruzzlings drop 3 at a time in Albrecht's Laboratories, or a rare Zariman bounty/container drop

conditions: Lanthorns are a Deimos resource, not a Zariman resource — Netracells are the reliable source; the Zariman bounty drop is only ~7.9% for 3.
Trading the blueprint skips the Rank 1 purchase, but not the Zariman-only build materials.
You may craft Innodem before Mastery Rank 14, but cannot equip it until then.

groups.meta: no Genesis adapter or Circuit rotation needed
groups.mode: solo recommended for Evolutions III and IV

rows.label: Incarnon Form activations in one mission
Heavy Attacks on Thrax Centurions or Legatus
Solo mission with an Incarnon weapon in every slot

conditions: Evolution I's combo must come from Innodem itself — charging it with an exalted weapon's combo counter (e.g. Ash's Bladestorm) does not work.
Evolutions III and IV don't reliably register progress as a client; run them solo.
Evolution IV has reported bugs (Jan/Apr 2026) where the rupture counter sticks; file a support ticket rather than grinding more Void Flood if it freezes.
Evolution V voids if an Exalted weapon is used; Incarnon Genesis (Circuit adapter) weapons do count.
bonuses: Pair with Laetum (1 Pinion, 5 Quill) and Felarx (10 Pinion, 15 Quill) for the cheapest 'Incarnon in every slot' combination for Evolution V.

disclosures.title: most people build it only for the challenge
disclosures.body: Innodem is the cheapest melee Incarnon in the game (5 Pinions/10 Quills against Praedos's 15/30), which is why it exists on most accounts primarily to satisfy Evolution V for other weapons. A 65-5 poll on whether it's top-3 melee went firmly against; most people keep Praedos equipped instead, for the parkour speed.
